## Context

The Democracy and Dictatorship (DD) data were released as part of TidyTuesday on November 5, 2024. TidyTuesday is a weekly project that shares open datasets for users to practice data analysis. This version updates the dataset from Bjørnskov and Rode (2020), building on earlier work by Cheibub et al. (2010) and Alvarez et al. (1996). The dataset was later cleaned and shared on GitHub by Jon Harmon. Bjørnskov and Rode expanded existing data on political regimes by adding more countries, institutional detail, and a clear indicator for both successful and failed coups. They defined coups using three criteria: the goal must be to overthrow the executive, the actors must be connected to the state, and the event must last no longer than a week. This provides a consistent way to identify and compare regime changes. The dataset focuses primarily on whether a country is democratic or not. Using this structure, we can study how often countries move away from democracy and how long those periods last which we call "spells." Building on this, our analysis applies unique visualization techniques and survival analysis methods to examine the duration and hazard of non-democratic spells.

## Research Questions

1.  How long on average does it take countries that stopped being democratic to return to democracy?
2.  What factors influence the breaking of a non-democratic spell?
